title: Collaborative Media Rendering Workflow
business: A boutique animation studio requiring shared access to large asset libraries across multiple compute instances.
problem: The studio struggled with data silos where individual rendering instances maintained local copies of assets, leading to inconsistent versions and high storage overhead.
solution: Amazon EFS provides a managed, elastic NFS file system that allows multiple compute instances to concurrently mount the same storage volume, ensuring a single source of truth for all rendering assets.
steps: Create an Amazon EFS file system within the VPC to serve as the centralized asset repository.
Configure mount targets in each Availability Zone where rendering instances are deployed.
Update the security group rules for the EFS mount targets to permit NFS traffic from the rendering instances.
Mount the EFS file system on each compute instance using the standard Linux mount command with the NFS protocol.
outcome: The studio achieves seamless collaboration as all rendering nodes access the same file system, eliminating the need for manual synchronization and reducing storage redundancy.
limitation: EFS performance is subject to throughput limits based on the file system size and burst credits; administrators can monitor this via CloudWatch metrics to ensure the workload does not exceed provisioned or burstable capacity.
